query: For W–Cu metal-matrix composites used in heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications, what single intervention could increase thermal conductivity while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite, defines the application conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of a High-entropy alloy (HEA) design with optimized composition and structure into W–Cu metal-matrix composites will increase thermal conductivity by 15% while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance under heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint application conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu metal-matrix composite used in heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications
generation.intervention: Incorporation of High-entropy alloy design with optimized composition and structure
generation.conditions: Heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications with operating temperatures up to 1000°C
generation.structural_mediator: Optimized composition and structure of the High-entropy alloy
generation.mechanism: Enhanced thermal conductivity due to optimized composition and structure, while retaining mechanical durability and irradiation resistance through the inherent properties of the High-entropy alloy
generation.baseline: Thermal conductivity of an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite without the High-entropy alloy design
generation.uncertainty: The actual increase in thermal conductivity may vary depending on the specific composition and structure of the High-entropy alloy, as well as the exact operating conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the thermal conductivity of W–Cu metal-matrix composites with and without the High-entropy alloy design under heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint application conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the W–Cu metal-matrix composite with the High-entropy alloy design is not at least 10% higher than that of the comparable composite without the High-entropy alloy design, the hypothesis is falsified
